summary.one_liner: fzf is a general-purpose command-line fuzzy finder and interactive terminal toolkit that reads lists from stdin and returns the selected item.
summary.what_it_does: fzf reads a list from STDIN (or walks the current directory if no pipe is given) and opens an interactive fuzzy-filter interface, writing the selected item to STDOUT. It supports extended search syntax with exact, prefix, suffix, inverse and OR terms, plus an exact-match mode via -e/--exact. Display modes include fullscreen, --height, and --popup (inside tmux 3.3+ or Zellij 0.44+). A preview window runs an external command on the focused line, with ANSI color and image display support. Key bindings, event-driven actions such as reload, become and execute let shell scripts turn into interactive terminal applications. Shell integration adds CTRL-T, CTRL-R and ALT-C bindings and fuzzy completion for bash, zsh, fish and Nushell, and there is a Vim/Neovim plugin.
use_cases: fuzzy-find files and directories in the terminal
search and reuse shell command history
preview file contents while choosing a file
build interactive menus in shell scripts
pipe ripgrep or find output into an interactive picker
fuzzy tab completion for paths, PIDs and hostnames
stack: Go (single binary, implied by distribution as a single binary)
notable: Distributed as a single binary and installable from many package managers across Linux, macOS, BSD and Windows
Shell integration via eval "$(fzf --bash)" for key bindings and fuzzy completion
become(...) action replaces the fzf process with another command, enabling multi-binding workflows
Interactive ripgrep pattern using reload bound to the change event
Preview window supports ANSI colors and image display via Kitty, iTerm2 or Sixel protocols
caveats: --popup requires tmux 3.3+ or Zellij 0.44+ and is ignored elsewhere
README warns against putting --preview in FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS
Custom completion API is described as experimental and subject to change
Nushell fuzzy completion requires version 0.116.1 or newer
